scope: Primary-source anchors for hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction and pressure-dependent recruitment/derecruitment. Quantitative model gates use broad mechanism-level targets unless an exact external scale is explicitly stated.

sources.name: Asadi et al. 2015
sources.title: Inhaled nitric oxide alters the distribution of blood flow in the healthy human lung, suggesting active hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction in normoxia
sources.use: Human evidence that HPV actively redistributes regional pulmonary perfusion and contributes to V/Q matching.

sources.name: Robin et al. 1987
sources.title: Hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction persists in the human transplanted lung
sources.use: Human evidence that global hypoxia increases pulmonary artery pressure and pulmonary vascular resistance even in denervated transplanted lungs.

sources.name: Crotti et al. 2001
sources.title: Recruitment and derecruitment during acute respiratory failure: a clinical study
sources.use: Human acute-respiratory-failure evidence that recruitment/derecruitment depends on PEEP, tidal inflation and regional superimposed pressure.

sources.name: Hammond et al. 1986
sources.title: Pulmonary gas exchange in humans during exercise at sea level
sources.use: MIGET anchor retained from v0.13: V/Q inequality increases during heavy exercise and diffusion limitation can emerge at high VO2.

nonclaims: The six-unit model is not a MIGET inversion.
The recruitment thresholds are not fitted to patient CT opening-pressure distributions.
PEEP in v0.14 is a reduced regional recruitment control state, not a complete mechanical-ventilator model.
HPV molecular signaling is not simulated; only its vascular control effect is represented.
